executiveSummary: GM0171's official 2025 identity, contained reference point, 50,788-resident control, forty-nine neighbourhoods, twelve BAG places, thirteen BRT settlements and ten logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Three BAG label centres lie just outside the independently generalized CBS boundary; this is an edition/geometry caveat, not evidence that Tollebeek, Espel or Creil is outside the municipality. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Noordoostpolder is a deeply drained, below-sea-level 48,000-hectare polder whose low and high divisions depend on Buma, Vissering and Smeenge pumping, a dense controlled-water system and primary defences. It directly borders IJsselmeer and Ketelmeer; Markermeer is an upstream IJsselmeer-system dependency and Zwarte Meer is connected across the Ramspol barrier, not a direct municipal shoreline. Official local planning scenarios say a selected Westermeerdijk breach can reach about four metres and make part of A6 impassable after twelve hours, while a Zuidermeerdijk breach can reach about 2.5 metres and affect A6 after six hours; depths elsewhere vary roughly 0.5–5 metres and water may remain for months. The simulator instead presents one persistent 2.961937-metre major-river surface across almost the whole municipality without a selected defence, breach, compartment, arrival, A6 state, recession or dewatering mechanism. Its direct North Sea coastal result is correctly narrow at zero depth but cannot be read as safety from IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer/Zwarte Meer-system or polder flooding. Pluvial outputs ignore the authority's 20/40 mm per 24-hour operating examples, municipal 70 mm per hour design test, catchments, inlet changes and pump state. Nine active hazard/component families reuse one neighbourhood seed; a controlled ignition in Kraggenburg-landelijk ranks its containing neighbourhood only about twenty-ninth by affected people. The logical graph also collapses A6/Ketelbrug, N50/Ramspolbrug, N331/N333 eastern crossings and dispersed-village access, and it omits external acute-care acceptance. Public context exposes 1,659 partial water/wastewater objects, one Kadoelen observation, four forecasts only through T+24, one Marknesse weather observation, one electricity-capacity planning sample and provider responsibility polygons. None supplies live topology, capacity compatibility, backup, staffing, stock, outage or restoration. Exact first-72-hour service, access, evacuation and recovery values must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until a selected event, physical dependencies and an accountable action/resource ledger are bound; NoData is never zero, open, safe or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0171 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0171 as Noordoostpolder in Flevoland and Veiligheidsregio Flevoland, with 50,788 residents, density 111/km², 19.1% aged 65 or older and 7,417 one-person households. The reference point [5.788956105781688,52.70821847808138] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Forty-nine neighbourhoods in twelve districts sum to 50,810 residents, twenty-two above the municipal control (+0.043%); published households total 21,675 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 9,725. Deterministic allocation subtracts twenty-two without rewriting source observations.

Bant, Creil, Emmeloord, Ens, Espel, Kraggenburg, Luttelgeest, Marknesse, Nagele, Rutten, Schokland and Tollebeek are the twelve BAG places. Thirteen BRT settlements comprise two buurtschappen and eleven woonkernen and additionally include Ketelhoek.

The Tollebeek, Espel and Creil BAG label points fall just outside the independently generalized polygon. Label-point/generalization mismatch requires full-resolution co-edition review and is not evidence of exclusion.

District-heating and public-charging values are null in all forty-nine neighbourhoods; ten housing/benefit fields cover 38/49, cars per household 35/49, average household size 48/49 and doctor/supermarket context 47/49. Null remains NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Concept-visie klimaatadaptatie and current Omgevingsvisie Noordoostpolder
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal climate-adaptation concept document, including Waterschap Zuiderzeeland 2011 flood-scenario references; Omgevingsvisie version 3.0 dated 30 September 2024; planning/context evidence, blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipal climate document says a breach can produce roughly 2–5 m inundation over much of the polder and 0.5–2 m near Urk/old land; the exact field depends on breach location. It describes a small annual place-based probability range, which is planning context and never an all-clear.

In cited 72-hour water-board scenarios a Westermeerdijk breach reaches about 4 m and makes part of A6 impassable after twelve hours; a Zuidermeerdijk breach reaches about 2.5 m and affects A6 after six hours. The polder may remain inundated for months.

The same document says its strategy did not develop a breach measure package because probability was considered small, while still requiring disaster/evacuation planning. Strategy choice is not proof of present readiness.

Current municipal vision describes Noordoostpolder as eighty years dry, a world-level agricultural municipality with soil-subsidence, climate, water-and-soil, tourism and A6/N50 accessibility challenges.

Agricultural workers, temporary labour migrants, visitors, livestock and businesses are operationally material but are not represented by the resident-only exposure surface; the inspected public records do not provide incident-time counts.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Rainwater design guidance and Noordoostpolder wet-weather operating examples
evidenceSources.edition: Current public water-board operating-context page and municipal LIOR water/riolering guidance inspected 3 September 2026; public examples/design criteria, not live incident commands; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The water board says Noordoostpolder has a smaller water system and therefore greater effects from heavy rain than eastern/southern Flevoland. With KNMI warnings it can pre-pump/lower canal levels and in very wet periods stop water inflow.

Its SMS examples distinguish 'Nat' at an expected 20 mm/24 h, reducing inflow and lowering various levels, from 'zeer Nat' at 40 mm/24 h, stopping inflow and lowering levels. Examples are not proof that any action is active.

Municipal public-space guidance designs water storage/overflow against T=100, 70 mm in one hour, and distinguishes road/floor freeboard and controlled discharge. This design test is not an observed storm or guaranteed no-damage threshold.

Pluvial consequence requires forecast/observation, catchment, ground level, soil saturation, sewer, canal target/current level, pump/inlet/outfall and power state. No single generic depth can substitute for that chain.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Noordoostpolder pumps, divisions and primary-defence lifecycle
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board pages inspected 3 September 2026; asset/function and HWBP lifecycle context; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The authority describes Noordoostpolder as 48,000 ha divided into a high and low division. Buma and Vissering remove excess water from the low division, while Smeenge serves the high division; Vissering discharges to IJsselmeer.

Water inlets are concentrated toward the north-east, can open automatically when levels are low and close during prolonged rain; they serve agriculture/nature and must not be confused with drinking water or drainage capacity.

A current HWBP page says Zuidermeerdijk is part of a 40 km trajectory protecting Noordoostpolder from IJsselmeer and that a roughly 1 km section associated with the future MSNF did not meet the norm and remains in plan/tender preparation. Lifecycle status is not a live failure or a whole-dike rating.

The Repelweg inlet in Kadoelermeerdijk was rejected for piping under design conditions and underwent a 2025 strengthening project with aftercare planned through April 2026. The page does not publish completion confirmation at audit time; it also says the inlet is closed in a very heavy storm.
No public page inspected supplies incident-time gate/pump state, achievable flow, power/backup, connected compartments, damage or dewatering completion.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — A6/Ketelbrug, N50/Ramspolbrug and Stormvloedkering Ramspol
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS asset and road pages inspected 3 September 2026; maintenance/lifecycle and structural context; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: RWS says the inflatable Ramspol barrier closes Zwarte Meer from Ketelmeer at NAP +0.50 m with strong north-westerly wind and that without it large parts of Noordoostpolder and Overijssel could flood. Zwarte Meer is therefore a cross-boundary system dependency, not a direct GM0171 shore.

A6 runs via Emmeloord and has Ketelbrug as one of its two movable bridges; N50 runs from Hattemerbroek to Emmeloord and includes Eilandbrug and Ramspolbrug. Road labels alone do not provide live crossing state.

A6 north and south logical edges are series directions of one corridor; N351's Urk and Steenwijkerland edges likewise share physical road. They must not be summed as independent evacuation or supply capacity.
RWS maintenance pages show 2026 A6 work and Ramspol-barrier internal work. Date-bounded lifecycle context needs live confirmation and cannot become a generic closure or availability value.
Markermeer is part of the wider IJsselmeer water system but is not a direct Noordoostpolder boundary; a selected event must preserve named water body, barrier, defence, direction and valid time.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Coördinatieplan Overstromingen Flevoland and document register
evidenceSources.edition: Flood coordination plan adopted 26 March 2009 and still exposed in the authority's document library beside Regionaal Crisisplan 2026–2029; old doctrine/scenario context, not evidence of current resources
supports: The plan phases worst-case flooding from T-120 to beyond T+24, including monitoring, zoning, inter-authority coordination, mobility, collection locations, energy, shelter/safe havens, communications, assistance, logistics and control measures.
Its extreme-rain scenario places major infrastructure damage and scarce emergency capacity through T+12 to T+96; worst-case storm/flood phase IV likewise runs T+24 to T+96.
A checklist or time target is not evidence that a location, route, shelter, vehicle, generator, crew, stock or communication channel is operational for a selected incident.
Because the detailed document was adopted in 2009, every organization, mandate, contact, site and resource requires current validation against the 2026–2029 crisis plan and incident command.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards and Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Partial water/wastewater register and Kadoelen observations/forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z, CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; Waterinfo observations retrieved 2026-09-02T18:03:18Z and forecasts 2026-09-03T04:29:19Z, CC0 unless component exception
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns 1,659 HWH objects to GM0171: twelve sewer pumps, two sluices, thirty surface-water pumps, one wastewater-treatment plant and 1,614 weirs. All sewer pumps and five surface-water pumps have a non-null capacity number; units/connectivity and live achievable flow remain unresolved.

Named context includes Buma and Smeenge, multiple inflow/underdrainage pumps and AWZI Tollebeek. 'Gerealiseerd' and register presence mean lifecycle/existence, not current control, power/backup or operability; Vissering lies outside GM0171 on Urk but is a real dependency.
The one local observation reports -22 cm NAP at Kadoelen Zwanediep at 2026-09-02T17:30Z. It is a point/time water level, not IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer/Zwarte Meer or polder state.

Four forecasts at that point give -24/-18/-13/-19 cm NAP at T+1/+6/+12/+24. No local T+48/T+72 point was returned. Point guidance is not an inundation surface or operating instruction; missing horizons remain NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: KNMI, Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RIVM, RDI and DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Timestamped weather, utility responsibility/planning and external-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; KNMI 10-minute observations v1.0, CC BY 4.0; source-specific licences/cadences
supports: Marknesse station 06273 observed 16.9°C, 87% relative humidity, wind 4.12 m/s, gust 6.31 m/s and 0.009 mm preceding-hour rain at 2026-09-02T23:30Z; station elevation is -3.35 m. This is a timestamped station observation, not a municipal field or T+72 forecast.

At the reference point public responsibility polygons return Liander for electricity/gas, Vitens for drinking water and Ziggo for media, with no drainage match. Polygons are responsibility context, not connectivity, topology, pressure, coverage quality, outage or restoration.

One 8305BM sample maps to Liander's Emmeloord installation 2+3 and reports 44 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 16.3 MW/51-request withdrawal queue, 44 MW existing and 38 MW required injection, and three projects with earliest 2031. It is large-user planning context, not live load, emergency reserve or municipal capacity.

No RIVM acute-care point lies inside GM0171. Isala Meppel is about 28.7 km and Frisius MC Heerenveen about 30.0 km straight-line from the reference point; their reported 24/7 emergency role does not establish ambulance/crossing access, staffing, diversion, backup or incident acceptance.

RDI assigns 131 sites/283 antennas and DUO 68 education locations. Zero local NDW situations, air stations, warnings, government-service points and recent seismic origins are scoped NoData, not open roads, normal conditions, available services or safety.

identity.summary: GM0171, Noordoostpolder, Flevoland and Veiligheidsregio Flevoland agree across generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The reference point lies inside the generalized 2025 geometry.
Administrative edition, old/current planning, lifecycle record, timestamped observation/forecast and synthetic exercise time remain separate.

geography.summary: Polder context is strong, but generalized edges and missing defence/compartment connectivity prevent hydraulic use.
notes: Three BAG-centre mismatches demonstrate that independently generalized geometry is not exact for border/water joins.
IJsselmeer and Ketelmeer are direct waters; Markermeer and Zwarte Meer are connected-system dependencies rather than direct GM0171 shores.
Use full-resolution administrative joins and authority defence, breach, polder, elevation, arrival/recession and pump geometry for consequences.

demography.summary: Registered residents reconcile, but workers, visitors and agricultural response populations are absent and Unknown.
notes: Published neighbourhood population is 50,810, twenty-two above the 50,788 control (+0.043%); deterministic reconciliation subtracts twenty-two.
The official control includes 19.1% aged 65+ and 7,417 one-person households, useful vulnerability context but not care demand.
Temporary workers, visitors, field staff, livestock owners and responders need timestamped, non-double-counted cohorts; no live count was found.

regionalDetail.summary: All forty-nine neighbourhoods are retained, but partial statistics and resident weighting omit polder compartments and dynamic rural activity.
notes: Emmeloord urban neighbourhoods dominate resident totals, but population size is not hydraulic, pluvial, wildfire or access exposure.
Large rural neighbourhoods combine farms, roads, nature, recreation and sparse residents and cannot be represented by one centre/multiplier.
Null district heating/charging and partial household/property fields remain NoData.

settlements.summary: Twelve BAG places and thirteen BRT settlements preserve the ring-village structure, subject to three generalized-boundary caveats.
notes: BRT adds Ketelhoek and separately labels two buurtschappen and eleven woonkernen; place and settlement concepts are not interchangeable.
Retain Tollebeek, Espel and Creil despite label points outside the generalized polygon.
Villages and education locations are not automatically shelters, distribution points or staffed support sites.

transport.summary: Ten border links omit physical crossing/common-cause state and cannot support rural evacuation, resupply or external care.
notes: A6 links Dronten and De Fryske Marren through one corridor, including Ketelbrug south; N50 reaches Kampen through Ramspolbrug. N331/N333 connect the old-land side and N351 connects Urk/Steenwijkerland.
Repeated route edges are series directions, not independent additive capacity; bridge, barrier, flooded-section and traffic states must propagate once.
No ProRail station exists; 74 GTFS stop areas are schedules, not vehicles/drivers, passable rural routes or evacuation capability.

emergencyContext.summary: Official scenarios define relevant decisions from pre-impact through T+96, but current event resources and completions are Unknown.
notes: Breach selection changes A6 loss from about six to twelve hours; warning/evacuation and rural-route decisions must begin before consequence display.
The detailed public flood plan is from 2009 and must be revalidated against current doctrine and command before operational use.
Shelters, transport, pumps, crossings, hospital acceptance, generators/fuel, water distribution, resupply, crews and restoration remain Unknown without incident confirmation.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six checkpoints across all eight services for GM0171.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 31.03 seconds, tests 30.80 seconds.
Diagnostic all-preset run passed one file/two tests in 14.74 seconds, tests 14.51 seconds; controlled Kraggenburg-landelijk ignition executed in 0.428 seconds.
Final focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 30.37 seconds, tests 30.13 seconds.
Execution coverage is not physical, spatial, population, network, operational or recovery calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, resident/demand/delivery reconciliation, determinism and cumulative-burden invariants hold for the resident-only model.
notes: All numeric outputs are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and no greater than the fixed 50,788 resident control.
Neighbourhood residents and service demand/delivery sums reconcile at every tested frame.
The invariant does not validate temporary-worker/visitor populations, physical capacity or displayed decimal precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded forty-nine-neighbourhood surface replaces breach, polder, rainfall, fire and infrastructure geography.
notes: Nine active preset/component families reuse one local hash rather than sampling mechanism-specific footprints.
River-flood exposure covers almost every neighbourhood without a breach, connected compartment, arrival or defence state.

A controlled ignition inside Kraggenburg-landelijk produces city flame 0.266232, smoke 0.561571 and 6,413 affected people, but its containing neighbourhood has only 91/725 affected and ranks about twenty-ninth by affected count.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability omits pumping divisions, water controls, crossings, dispersed villages, external care and operator state.
notes: The 1,659 partial HWH objects and five local water records remain display context and do not drive pump/inlet/weir/sluice/WWTP connectivity, receiving level, power/backup or dewatering.
One logical road graph is insufficient for A6/Ketelbrug, N50/Ramspolbrug, eastern crossings, rural roads, bus continuity and hospital routes.
Provider polygons, one planning sample, antennas/schools and external annual hospital records do not calibrate live availability, capacity, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers reconcile, but mechanism, population and operational provenance do not support displayed precision.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.

River T+24 reports severity 0.918504, depth 2.961937, 28,531 affected and 515,103 person-hours; the depth lies within an official broad scenario range but has no selected breach or spatial field and is therefore false precision.
Coastal T+24 reports exact depth zero, zero affected and 48,953 person-hours: retain only direct North Sea scope and label burden as indirect synthetic, not local coastal safety.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 affected, service and burden trajectories are not driven by confirmed polder, route, evacuation or repair actions.
notes: River depth/severity remain 2.961937/0.918504 while affected rises 28,531→29,516 and burden 515,103→2,007,386; seven service values freeze and Facilities falls without a governed action state.
Compound depth remains 0.526777 while affected rises 29,810→31,592 and burden 537,002→2,192,896; seven services barely change and Facilities falls without resources or blockers.

Official local planning says breach water may remain for months, Waterinfo local forecast coverage stops at T+24, and no source confirms T+72 pumping, route clearance, evacuation, care acceptance, resupply or restoration.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, centre containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM0171/Noordoostpolder/Flevoland/VRF, the contained reference point and a twenty-two-resident (+0.043%) neighbourhood rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 edition, exact nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: Three BAG label points fall outside the generalized CBS polygon and water-system boundaries require precise scope.
findings.evidence: E01 shows Tollebeek, Espel and Creil label centres outside the independently generalized boundary. E04/E05 distinguish direct IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer edges from connected Markermeer/Zwarte Meer dependencies.
findings.action: Retain all places and the caveat; use full-resolution co-edition geometry and explicitly name direct versus connected waters.

findings.summary: A plausible scalar flood depth becomes false precision without a selected defence breach, compartment or arrival field.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports exact depth 2.961937 and severity 0.918504 across almost all neighbourhoods. E02 says Westermeerdijk and Zuidermeerdijk cases differ in depth and make A6 impassable after about twelve versus six hours, with water potentially remaining for months.
findings.action: Require a versioned IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer/Ramspol/defence event with named failure/overtopping, boundary/datum, connected polder, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, A6 state, pumping and uncertainty before local consequence.

findings.summary: Direct North Sea coastal zero is narrowly correct but can be misread as no lake-system or polder flood risk.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 gives exact depth/affected zero while accumulating 48,953 person-hours. E02/E04/E05 establish primary defences, IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer exposure and Ramspol/Zwarte Meer dependency, not a direct North Sea shore or direct Markermeer boundary.
findings.action: Retain direct North Sea zero only with explicit source scope; route selected lake/defence cases through a dedicated polder-flood mechanism and preserve unsampled pathways as Unknown.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial and storm residual depths ignore published rain tests and active water-control decisions.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports rain zero, depth 0.190280 and 5,752 affected; severe storm reports rain/wind zero but residual depth 0.474239. E03 distinguishes 20/40 mm per 24-hour operational examples and a municipal 70 mm/hour design test, with pre-pumping/inflow changes.
findings.action: Bind timestamped rain to AHN/BGT, soil, catchments, sewer/canal/pump/inlet/outfall/receiving level and power state; display design scenario, observation, forecast and synthetic exercise separately.

findings.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed and failed source containment replace mechanism-specific geography.
findings.evidence: Nine active families reuse one forty-nine-neighbourhood hash. Controlled fire in Kraggenburg-landelijk yields city flame 0.266232/smoke 0.561571 and 6,413 affected, but its containing area gets 91/725 and ranks about twenty-ninth.
findings.action: Use hazard-specific breach/pluvial/wind/heat/fire/plume/cyber surfaces; require eligible fuel, source containment, valid-time weather, road/water access and suppression state for wildfire.

findings.summary: The distinctive high/low pumping, inlet, defence and wastewater system does not causally drive Water or Drainage.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 identify Buma–Vissering–Smeenge and pre-pump/inlet decisions; E07 exposes 1,659 partial assets but unresolved units/connectivity and forecasts only through T+24. Exact T+24 river Water 0.477493 and Drainage 0.292876 have no operator state.
findings.action: Integrate authority-reviewed compartments, flows/units, controls, outfalls/receiving levels, sewer/AWZI, power/backup and valid-time aggregate state where publishable; otherwise affectsSimulation=false and Unknown.

findings.summary: A6/N50/eastern crossing state, rural-village access and external acute care are absent from first-72-hour continuity.
findings.evidence: E02 gives breach-specific A6 loss at six/twelve hours; E05 identifies Ketelbrug/Ramspolbrug and common corridors. The graph has ten border edges but no physical crossing state, and E08 shows no local acute-care point with nearest reported 24/7 options outside the municipality.
findings.action: Represent crossings and flooded road sections once with direction/mode/time/common cause; route village evacuation, mutual aid, supply and hospital transfer with traffic, vehicles, ambulance and destination acceptance or leave state Unknown.

findings.summary: Resident-only allocation omits temporary labour, agricultural/seasonal activity, visitors, responders and livestock dependencies.
findings.evidence: E01 caps exposure at 50,788 residents; E02 describes a globally significant agricultural economy, temporary-labour housing demand and expanding tourism. No inspected public source gives incident-time people or livestock by field, farm, accommodation or attraction.
findings.action: Add separately sourced, timestamped resident, registered-worker/guest, estimated day/field and responder cohorts plus livestock/animal-rescue demand; never turn missing occupancy into zero.

findings.summary: Provider polygons, one capacity sample and public registers cannot calibrate exact utility/care availability.
findings.evidence: E08 supplies Liander/Vitens/Ziggo responsibility, one large-user planning sample, 131 antenna sites, 68 schools and external hospital records but no live topology, load/pressure/quality/outage, backhaul, backup, staffing, stock or restoration.
findings.action: Label percentages synthetic; ingest only authorised timestamped aggregate incident evidence, preserve sensitive topology constraints and keep no-match/null/sample values Unknown rather than municipal totals.

findings.summary: Point observations, forecast gaps and zero record counts need explicit coverage and evidence-class labels.
findings.evidence: E07 has one Kadoelen observation and forecasts through T+24 only; E08 has one Marknesse station but zero local warnings/air/NDW/government/seismic records. None means whole-polder conditions, normality, open routes or safety.
findings.action: Show publisher/version/licence, issue/valid/expiry time, location, units/datum, quality, coverage and evidence class; distinguish modeled zero, NoData, Unknown, not applicable and indirect synthetic effect.

findings.summary: First-72-hour evacuation, service and recovery changes lack accountable local actions, resources and blockers.
findings.evidence: River and compound burdens reach 2,007,386 and 2,192,896 person-hours while depths/services largely freeze and Facilities changes. E02 says inundation may last months; E06 is doctrine, E07 stops local forecasts at T+24, and no source confirms pumping, crossing, shelter, care, fuel, water, resupply or repair completion.
findings.action: Add a T0/6/12/24/48/72 incident/action/resource/blocker ledger with actor, proposal/request/confirmation/dispatch/active/completion, location, capacity, dependency, valid/expiry time and uncertainty; suppress unconfirmed recovery attribution.

residualLimitations: No inspected public source supplies a complete current defence, breach, polder-compartment, sewer/control and dewatering model with event-time state suitable for direct simulation.
No safe-to-publish Liander/Vitens/gas/telecom topology, live state, backup endurance, priority users, crews or restoration estimate was found; responsibility polygons are not networks.
The HWH aggregation is partial and capacity units/connectivity remain incomplete; registered existence is not operating state and unlisted assets may not be inferred absent.
One Kadoelen observation and four forecasts through T+24 retain point/time validity only; absence at T+48/T+72 is NoData and does not describe IJsselmeer, Ketelmeer, Zwarte Meer or polder water.
No governed feed supplies live temporary-worker, visitor, field, livestock, shelter/evacuation or responder occupancy; municipal planning importance is not a count.
The public detailed flood coordination plan is dated 2009; its roles, sites, resources and timings require current validation and cannot be treated as incident completion.
NWB nominal capacities are generalized scenario units; they do not establish bridge, road, evacuation, hospital or supply throughput.
Exact local hazard, affected, service, person-hour and recovery values remain synthetic until authority-reviewed events, populations, physical dependencies and operational actions are bound.
provinceReviewFlags: Municipality release blocker: replace GM0171's generic persistent major-river field with authority-selected IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer/defence and polder-compartment cases; preserve all unselected mechanisms as Unknown, never safe.
Review direct geography once across Flevoland: Noordoostpolder borders IJsselmeer/Ketelmeer, while Markermeer and Zwarte Meer/Ramspol are connected system dependencies, not interchangeable shores.

Coordinate Westermeerdijk, Zuidermeerdijk, Kadoelermeerdijk/Repelweg and Ramspol lifecycle/event state with Zuiderzeeland/RWS; planned work or norm assessment is not live failure or completed strengthening.
Model A6/Ketelbrug, N50/Ramspolbrug, N331/N333 and N351 route segments as non-additive shared assets with breach, wind, maintenance and traffic state across Flevoland, Overijssel, Fryslân and Urk.

Coordinate Isala Meppel, Frisius MC Heerenveen and alternates as external acute-care destinations with ambulance route, staffing, diversion/acceptance and backup rather than generic Facilities percentages.
